plain.text: David sang this when the LORD rescued him from his enemies and from King Saul. "I love you, LORD, my strength. The LORD is my rock, my fortress and my deliverer; my God is my rock, in whom I take refuge, my shield and my stronghold. I called to the LORD, who is worthy of praise, and I was saved from my enemies."

The cords of death tangled around him and floods of destruction overwhelmed him. In his distress he called to the LORD, and God heard from his temple. David describes God coming to save him in a mighty storm: the earth trembled, smoke and fire, thunder and lightning, dark clouds under his feet. God reached down from on high, took hold of him and drew him out of deep waters. He rescued him from a powerful enemy. "He brought me out into a spacious place; he rescued me because he delighted in me."

David says God rewarded him for his faithfulness. To the faithful God shows himself faithful, and he saves the humble but brings down the proud. "You, LORD, keep my lamp burning; my God turns my darkness into light. With your help I can advance against a troop; with my God I can scale a wall." God's way is perfect, and his word is flawless.

"Who is God besides the LORD? And who is the Rock except our God?" God arms David with strength, makes his feet like those of a deer, trains his hands for battle, and gives him a shield of victory. "Your help has made me great." David describes defeating his enemies and becoming a leader over nations.

"The LORD lives! Praise be to my Rock! Exalted be God my Saviour!" God gives David victory and saves him. "Therefore I will praise you, LORD, among the nations." God gives great victories to his king and shows unfailing love to David and his descendants forever.

summary.bigIdea: David praises God as his rock and rescuer, who heard his cry and brought him out into a spacious place.
points: "The LORD is my rock, my fortress and my deliverer."
God came down to rescue David "because he delighted in me".
"My God turns my darkness into light."
summary.reflection: David piles up pictures of God: rock, fortress, shield, lamp. Which picture speaks to you most today, and why?
